newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico airport sell-offs to start this year-report.
newsitem.headline: Mexico airport sell-offs to start this year-report.

text.p: The process of privatizing Mexico's airports will begin toward the end of this year, the state news agency Notimex reported Sunday.

Quoting an unnamed official with the government agency Airports and Auxiliary Services, Notimex said 10 major airports would be part of the first wave of privatizations in 1997, naming airports in Mexico City, Cancun, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, Merida, los Cabos, Acapulco and Vercruz.

Foreign companies will be allowed to own up to 49 percent of the airports, the story said, adding that Mexican airlines Mexicana and Aeromexico were among the Mexican companies interested in some of the concessions.
The concessions, which would be for 50 years with a 50-year option should the airports be run efficiently, would hand over auxiliary services, cleaning and fuel distribution, Notimex said.
But the control towers, runways and airspace would remain in state hands.
The Mexico City airport is the largest up for privatization as it handles 629 commercial flights and nearly 42,000 passengers a day, Notimex said.
The first step toward airport privatization began in May with the publication of the Civil Aviation law, Notimex said.
